Prologue - The Hunt: New Technologies

Mikey had been working months to perfect the pinnacle of his engineering career. Known as Project Hijack, the work had been commissioned by Hest Security, a private security contractor. Mikey was recruited to Hest for his brilliant work in Computer Science - a field Hest was highly vested in for protecting the identities of it's clients. More specifically Hest was interested in Mikey's graduate work at Massachusetts Institute of Technology on Discrete Packet Injection - the ability to send data through previously created and encrypted packets that were being transmitted over wireless data. Although Mikey's research showed promise, it was roadblocked by MIT when they determined the technology could potentially devastate the world's digital infrastructure, and they did not want to risk the association. In short, Mikey was working on a device that could be used to connect a device to every piece of data in the immediate area - all 1's and 0's floating around on any wifi, bluetooth, or wireless network. The ramifications were vast, including the ability to scramble, read, and modify any digital communication - all without the need of a password. Hest, and almost every software company on earth tried to requisition Mikey for their own digital research, but only Hest provided the amount of funding and resources that Mikey would need to realize the full potential of his disruptive new technology. And so they hired Mikey, gave him a research team, and a high-security facility in San Francisco, California.

Mikey was working on one of the few final problems of his creation, not many could keep up with the intensive timeline set by Hest, but Mikey would work 100 hours a week if it meant realizing his creation. Co-workers had come and gone, but Tim had stuck with him through and through. Tim was a self-proclaimed hacktivist, he could detect patterns from thin air, and had taken down more than a handful of retail websites through sheer talent by the time he was 20. More importantly, he was Mikey's best friend. It was hard to convince Hest to take Tim; Hest considered hiring a well known hacker with strong ideals a risk to their internal data, but when Mikey threatened to pack up and take his research to Google, Hest was quick to pretend that their issues with Tim never existed. Tim was working from home this week, the official story was he had come down with the flu, but in reality, it was Mikey who had desired that he stay home and work. The side-project Mikey and Tim had devised was almost as devious as Project Hijack itself. It was a hack into the NSA that would give a best guess associative name, address, and profile picture from a persons social media account to an IP address. It was thought of a a strong companion Project Hijack, not only could you bear witness to all digital communications, you could also be given the name, address, and image of the person sending the data.

Mikey and Tim had devised the side project drunk at Tim's apartment late one night. They were playing Call of Duty when "faggot" was shouted one too many times by another player on the team while Mikey was playing. Tim became red and started shouting through the mic, "One day I'm gonna fucking track you the fuck down, and you wont even know it. I will scrub every website to find you, your address, and what your greatest fucking fear is. I will stick my dick in data and it will end up so far up your ass that it will turn you into the faggot you fear!" Mikey turned to Tim after his rant and asked, "Could you really do that?", "Turn him gay?" Tim replied. "No! Could you actually find him through an automated data scrubber?" Tim paused for a moment and thought deeply about the question, "Yes I suppose, although it would be far easier to just hack the Xbox database, get his name, address, credit card info, anything you want really - we could even do it for every Xbox user, we could create a mobile app for ourselves that could give us a bio of every faggot-flinging fucker we encounter while we play." Mikey looked at him intently, showing a sly smile. Before a second passed Tim had an overwhelming realization, he began pacing the room as he began to talk, "Mikey your fucking brilliant, why limit ourself to people playing Xbox, when we will have a device that will show the data of every device in an area, including the IP address. With that we can know who is sending the data, regardless of if the data itself contains any identification." Mikey could barely contain the erection that Tim had given him. Between the anti-homophobic rage and the discovering of a new use for software that could change the world, Mikey was feeling overwhelmed. It didn't help the matter that he knew Tim was gay as well. Mikey had to use one of the pillows on the sofa to "hide" it. It's not that Mikey didn't want a relationship with Tim, quite the contrary, Tim was Mikey's dream guy. It was just that whenever Mikey thought about coming out, he dreaded and overthought the complications that might ensue. He starts considering how his family life might change, he becomes scared of what friends he might lose, and he dreads the though that after all that emotional trauma, Tim might not even reciprocate the feelings. So they drank the night away while hacking away on their new side project. One that they both agreed was too dangerous to include in Project Hijack, more specifically, too dangerous to put in the hands of Hest.

End Prologue
